23 What is the approximate range of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation visible to the human
eye?
A
(430–750) kHz
B
(430–750) MHz
C
(430–750) GHz
D
(430–750) THz

hints: Notice all four options use the same numbers 430-750 but different prefixes kHz, MHz, GHz and THz - so recall the visible wavelengths in $\text{nm}$.
Connect wavelength to frequency with $c = f\lambda$ using $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\lambda \approx 400-700 \text{ nm}$.
Calculate $f = c/\lambda$ for the two ends and convert $10^{12} \text{ Hz} = 1 \text{ THz}$ to see which prefix fits.
walkthrough: Recall the visible spectrum is roughly $\lambda \approx 400 \text{ nm}$ for violet to $\lambda \approx 700 \text{ nm}$ for red, where $1 \text{ nm} = 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
Use the wave equation for electromagnetic waves in vacuum, $c = f\lambda$, so $f = c/\lambda$ with $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Since $1 \text{ THz} = 10^{12} \text{ Hz}$, this is $(430-750) \text{ THz}$, which is much larger than kHz, MHz or GHz radio and microwave frequencies. This is option D.

A.explanation: Frequencies of order $10^5 \text{ Hz}$ are radio waves, about $10^9$ times too small for visible light.

B.explanation: Frequencies of order $10^8 \text{ Hz}$ are radio waves, about $10^6$ times too small for visible light.

C.explanation: Frequencies of order $10^{11} \text{ Hz}$ are microwaves or infrared, about $10^3$ times too small for visible light.

D.explanation: Frequencies of order $10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ follow from $f = c/\lambda$ with visible wavelengths $400-700 \text{ nm}$.
